title: The Lord on the Throne
summary: Isaiah sees the Lord seated upon a high throne in the temple, with the Lord’s train filling it and seraphim above.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the Lord’s train filled the temple.
Seraphim stood above; each had six wings, covering face and feet with four and flying with two.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The throne is elevated inside the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s physical appearance and clothing are not described.
The seraphim’s appearance beyond their six wings is not described.
The temple’s architecture and furnishings are not described.

narration.text: In the year that king Uzziah died

prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Lord an appearance beyond the details stated.

title: The Seraph’s Cry
summary: One seraph cries to another; the doorposts move and smoke fills the temple.

explicit_facts.text: One seraph cried to another, declaring the Lord of Hosts holy and the whole earth full of his glory.
The doorposts moved at the voice of the one who cried, and the house filled with smoke.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Smoke is visible within the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The smoke’s appearance and the temple’s design are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: One seraph

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earth being full of glory is part of the seraph’s proclamation, not a described visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earth itself visibly filled with glory.

title: The Speaker’s Lament
summary: The speaker laments being undone and having unclean lips, says he dwells among a people of unclean lips, and says he has seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he is undone and is a man of unclean lips.
The speaker says he dwells among a people of unclean lips.
The speaker says his eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s appearance and surroundings are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wo is unto me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips; and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unnamed speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse says the speaker has seen the King, the Lord of Hosts; it does not describe that figure’s appearance or say the figure is visibly present while the speaker talks.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the people mentioned as physically present.
Do not invent an appearance for the King, the Lord of Hosts.
Do not assign a location not stated in the supplied verse.

title: The Live Coal
summary: A seraph flies to Isaiah with a live coal taken from the altar and lays it upon his mouth.

explicit_facts.text: A seraph flew to Isaiah with a live coal taken with tongs from the altar.
The seraph laid the coal upon Isaiah’s mouth and said his iniquity was taken away and his sin purged.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The altar and tongs are visible in the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The altar’s design and the coal’s color are unspecified.
The seraph’s appearance beyond its wings is unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lo, this has touched thy lips;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Seraph

spoken_dialogue.text: and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Seraph

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text describes the coal touching Isaiah’s mouth, not causing injury.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show burns, blood, or injury.

title: Isaiah Answers
summary: The Lord asks whom to send, and Isaiah offers himself.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah hears the Lord ask whom to send and who will go for them; Isaiah answers, offering himself.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Isaiah remains in the temple while hearing and answering.
unspecified_visual_details: No new appearance of the Lord is described in this verse.

spoken_dialogue.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Here am I; send me.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s voice is heard; the verse does not specify a new visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent another speaker or a new form for the Lord.

title: The Commission
summary: The Lord commissions Isaiah to tell the people that they hear and see without understanding or perceiving.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells Isaiah to go and tell the people; they hear without understanding and see without perceiving.
The Lord speaks of the people’s hearts, ears, and eyes, and their not understanding, converting, and being healed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord’s words can be heard off-screen while Isaiah listens in the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The people Isaiah is commissioned to address are not described as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: Go and tell this people
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Hear ye indeed, but they understood not;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and see ye indeed, but they perceived not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Make the heart of this people fat,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and make their ears heavy,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and shut their eyes
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted and be healed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The heart, ears, and eyes language is figurative; it does not describe physical changes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict organs changing or being supernaturally closed.

title: How Long?
summary: Isaiah asks how long, and the Lord answers with a prediction of desolation and removal.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah asks the Lord how long.
The Lord says cities will be wasted without inhabitants, houses without people, and the land desolate.
The Lord says people will be removed far away and there will be a great forsaking in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord’s answer can be heard off-screen while Isaiah listens in the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The predicted desolation and removal are not shown as present events.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lord, how long?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

spoken_dialogue.text: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and the houses without man,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and the land be utterly desolate;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And the Lord have removed men far away,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord describes future desolation and removal, not events happening in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the predicted desolation or removal as present action.

title: The Holy Seed
summary: The Lord describes a tenth that will return and compares what remains to a tree after its leaves are cast.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says there shall be a tenth; they shall return, and the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.
The Lord compares it to a teil-tree and an oak whose substance remains when they cast their leaves.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord’s words can be heard off-screen while Isaiah listens in the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of the tenth and holy seed are unspecified.
The verse does not describe a tree or returning people as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: But yet there shall be a tenth,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and they shall return,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: as a teil-tree,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and as an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees are a comparison, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a tree consuming people or stage a future return.
